title: UNIT 8: VECTORS IN TWO DIMENSIONS
notes:
✓ Vector → a quantity with BOTH magnitude and direction.

✓ Scalar → a quantity with magnitude ONLY.

✓ Key idea: Vector = size + direction | Scalar = size only.

title: 8.1 VECTOR & SCALAR QUANTITIES
notes:
◆ Scalars → mass, density, temperature, distance, area, speed.

◆ Vectors → force, velocity, acceleration, displacement, electric field, magnetic field.

✓ Remember: Speed is scalar, while velocity is vector.

title: VECTOR REPRESENTATION
notes:
✓ A vector is represented by a directed line segment AB⃗.

◆ A → initial point
◆ B → terminal point
◆ |AB⃗| → magnitude (length) of the vector
◆ Arrowhead → shows the direction

✓ The same vector can be moved without changing its magnitude or direction.

title: EQUAL, OPPOSITE & PARALLEL VECTORS
notes:
✓ Equal vectors → same magnitude + same direction.

✓ Opposite vectors → same magnitude + opposite directions.

✓ Parallel vectors → same or opposite direction.

✓ Two vectors are parallel if one is a scalar multiple of the other:
b⃗ = k a⃗

title: 8.2 REPRESENTATION OF A VECTOR
notes:
✓ A vector in two dimensions can be written as:

a⃗ = (x, y)

◆ x → horizontal component
◆ y → vertical component

✓ The components describe how far the vector moves horizontally and vertically.

title: MAGNITUDE OF A VECTOR
notes:
✓ For a⃗ = (x, y):

|a⃗| = √(x² + y²)

✓ For A(x₁,y₁) and B(x₂,y₂):

|AB⃗| = √[(x₂−x₁)² + (y₂−y₁)²]

✓ Magnitude = length of the vector.

title: DIRECTION OF A VECTOR
notes:
✓ The direction of a vector is given by the angle it makes with a reference direction.

For components x and y:

tan θ = y/x

✓ when θ is measured from the positive horizontal direction.

✓ Direction can also be expressed using bearings, such as:
N 53° E | S 45° W

title: 8.3 VECTOR ADDITION
notes:
◆ Triangle Law
If:
AB⃗ = u⃗ and BC⃗ = v⃗

then:
✓ AB⃗ + BC⃗ = AC⃗

✓ AC⃗ → resultant vector

◆ Method: Place the initial point of the second vector at the terminal point of the first vector.

title: PARALLELOGRAM LAW
notes:
✓ When two vectors start from the same point, complete a parallelogram using the two vectors.

✓ The diagonal represents the resultant:
R⃗ = u⃗ + v⃗

✓ For perpendicular vectors:
|R⃗| = √(|u⃗|² + |v⃗|²)

✓ This is based on Pythagoras' theorem.

title: VECTOR SUBTRACTION
notes:
✓ Subtracting a vector is the same as adding its opposite.

u⃗ − v⃗ = u⃗ + (−v⃗)

✓ Opposite vector → same magnitude but reversed direction.

✓ Think: subtraction = addition of the opposite.

title: ZERO VECTOR
notes:
✓ A zero (null) vector has:

Magnitude = 0
No definite direction

✓ Symbol: 0⃗

title: 8.3.2 SCALAR MULTIPLICATION
notes:
✓ For scalar k and vector a⃗:

ka⃗ changes the magnitude by a factor of |k|.

◆ k > 0 → same direction
◆ k < 0 → opposite direction
◆ |k| > 1 → vector becomes longer
◆ 0 < |k| < 1 → vector becomes shorter
◆ k = 0 → zero vector

title: 8.4 POSITION VECTOR
notes:
✓ A position vector starts at the origin O(0,0).

If its terminal point is (x,y):

u⃗ = xi + yj = (x,y)

◆ i = (1,0) → unit vector in x-direction
◆ j = (0,1) → unit vector in y-direction

title: VECTOR FROM TWO POINTS
notes:
If:
A = (x₁,y₁)
B = (x₂,y₂)

✓ then the vector from A to B is:

AB⃗ = (x₂−x₁, y₂−y₁)

✓ Final point − Initial point.

title: UNIT VECTORS i & j
notes:
✓ i = (1,0) → unit vector in the x-direction.
✓ j = (0,1) → unit vector in the y-direction.

Therefore:
u⃗ = xi + yj

i and j form the basic directions used to express 2D vectors.

title: 8.5 APPLICATIONS OF VECTORS
notes:
✓ Vectors are used to find or describe:

Displacement
Resultant forces
Horizontal & vertical components
Motion
Direction

✓ For perpendicular horizontal and vertical movements:
Displacement = √(horizontal² + vertical²)

✓ Vectors are useful whenever both SIZE and DIRECTION matter.

title: UNIT 8: FORMULA CHEAT SHEET
notes:
◆ Vector:
✓ a⃗ = (x,y)

◆ Magnitude:
✓ |a⃗| = √(x²+y²)

◆ Vector between two points:
✓ AB⃗ = (x₂−x₁,y₂−y₁)

◆ Distance / magnitude:
✓ |AB⃗| = √[(x₂−x₁)²+(y₂−y₁)²]

◆ Addition:
✓ u⃗ + v⃗ = resultant

◆ Subtraction:
✓ u⃗ − v⃗ = u⃗ + (−v⃗)

◆ Scalar multiplication:
✓ k(x,y) = (kx,ky)

◆ Position vector:
✓ u⃗ = xi+yj

◆ Perpendicular resultant:
✓ |R⃗| = √(|u⃗|²+|v⃗|²)

◆ Direction:
✓ tan θ = y/x

✓ EXAM TIP: Know the difference between scalar/vector, magnitude/direction, and initial/final coordinates.
